title: 3470. Permutations IV

examples.explanation: The lexicographically-sorted alternating permutations of [1, 2, 3, 4] are: [1, 2, 3, 4] [1, 4, 3, 2] [2, 1, 4, 3] [2, 3, 4, 1] [3, 2, 1, 4] [3, 4, 1, 2] ← 6th permutation [4, 1, 2, 3] [4, 3, 2, 1] Since k = 6, we return [3, 4, 1, 2].
The lexicographically-sorted alternating permutations of [1, 2, 3] are: [1, 2, 3] [3, 2, 1] ← 2nd permutation Since k = 2, we return [3, 2, 1].
The lexicographically-sorted alternating permutations of [1, 2] are: [1, 2] [2, 1] There are only 2 alternating permutations, but k = 3, which is out of range. Thus, we return an empty list [].
